name: Changsha Huanghua International Airport
before:
The busiest airport in central China, about 25 km from downtown Changsha at Huanghua, and the arrival point for the wider metropolitan region taking in Zhuzhou and Xiangtan.

Terminal 2 is the main building and a genuinely impressive one: 212,000 square metres, the fifth largest airport terminal in mainland China, with 22 air bridge gates and the longest walk from entrance to gate kept within 300 metres, which is unusually considerate for a terminal this size. Its main hall is the largest single steel truss structure in Hunan.

Terminal 1 reopened in May 2018 after a long renovation and now handles Air China, Shandong, Shenzhen, Tibet, Kunming, Chengdu, Joy Air and Okay Airways, with 38 check in counters and ten air bridges.

Between them the two terminals are rated for 15.6 million passengers a year.

The airport opened in August 1989, replacing Changsha Datuopu, which is now a military air base. It is run by the Hunan Airport Authority, which manages all five airports in the province.
after:
Hunan's busiest airport lies about 25 km from downtown Changsha at Huanghua and is the arrival point for the wider metropolitan region taking in Zhuzhou and Xiangtan.

Terminal 2 is the main building and a genuinely impressive one: 212,000 square metres, designed so that the longest walk to a gate is within 300 metres, which is unusually considerate for a terminal this size.

Air China flies from Terminal 1, which reopened in May 2018 after a long renovation.

The airport handled 30.3 million passengers in 2025, fifteenth in China.

claims.claim: 30.3 million passengers in 2025, fifteenth in China
claims.inAfter: The airport handled 30.3 million passengers in 2025, fifteenth in China.
claims.note: Replaces the old passenger figure, 'rated for 15.6 million passengers a year' (see the cut below): a capacity misread from Wikipedia and half the traffic the airport now carries. CAAC: 30,253,675, 15th, down 3.1 per cent on 31,218,109 in 2024.

sources.quote: Row 长沙/黄花: passenger rank 15 in China; passengers 2025: 30,253,675
As for 2025, Changsha Huanghua International Airport was the 15th busiest airport in the People's Republic of China with 30,253,675 passengers.

claims.claim: the busiest airport in central China
claims.wasBefore: The busiest airport in central China
claims.why: Wrong for 2024 and 2025: CAAC's table puts Wuhan ahead (31,339,277 against 30,253,675 in 2025; 31,406,186 against 31,218,109 in 2024). Wikipedia's 'busiest in Central China' is dated 2022. Replaced by Hunan's busiest (CAAC, Air China); Changsha's second place in central China rests on CAAC alone, so it is not stated.

claims.claim: fifth largest airport terminal in mainland China
claims.wasBefore: the fifth largest airport terminal in mainland China
claims.why: A 2011 ranking, long overtaken by newer terminals, and the two sources disagree on which four were larger (CNR: Beijing, Shanghai Hongqiao, Shanghai Pudong, Guangzhou; Wikipedia: Beijing Capital, Pudong, Guangzhou, Shenzhen).

claims.claim: 22 air bridge gates
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; CNR gives 47 stands across the airport, 75 per cent at the terminal, not a count of air bridges.

claims.claim: largest single steel truss structure in Hunan
claims.wasBefore: Its main hall is the largest single steel truss structure in Hunan.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. CNR (2011) calls T2 Hunan's most structurally complex and most modern public building, which is a different claim.

claims.claim: Terminal 1 airlines other than Air China
claims.wasBefore: now handles Air China, Shandong, Shenzhen, Tibet, Kunming, Chengdu, Joy Air and Okay Airways
claims.why: Time-sensitive and resting on Wikipedia alone for the seven airlines other than Air China; the operator's site did not connect and the Hunan Airport Group's refused (403). Air China is kept on its own current guide. CAOP's undated page (figures to 2017) says China Southern and XiamenAir have operating bases here; not added, as nothing dated within the year says so.

claims.claim: 38 check-in counters and ten air bridges
claims.wasBefore: with 38 check in counters and ten air bridges
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the 2018 Hunan Daily report it cites refused a plain fetch and the browser (403).

claims.claim: two terminals rated for 15.6 million passengers a year
claims.wasBefore: Between them the two terminals are rated for 15.6 million passengers a year.
claims.why: A misreading: Wikipedia gives 15.6 million as the capacity Terminal 2 ADDED in 2011, and six million for Terminal 1 alone after 2018; CNR (2011) says T2 lifted the airport from 4.6 million to more than 20 million a year. The airport carried 30.3 million in 2025 (CAAC), so the figure misleads. Replaced by the 2025 total.

claims.claim: opened August 1989, replacing Datuopu, now a military air base
claims.wasBefore: The airport opened in August 1989, replacing Changsha Datuopu, which is now a military air base.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The pages it cites could not be read: huaxia.com (no DNS answer), CAAC News (503), the Changsha government's English site (no connection), China Aviation Daily (503). CAOP dates only the opening of the air port of entry (1990).

claims.claim: run by the Hunan Airport Authority, which manages all five airports in the province
claims.wasBefore: It is run by the Hunan Airport Authority, which manages all five airports in the province.
claims.why: Out of date: CAAC's 2025 table lists ten Hunan airports with traffic, not five, and Wikipedia's own infobox names the operator as Hunan Airport Management Group Co., Ltd. The group's sites did not answer (csa.hnjcjt.com no connection, hnjcjt.com 403), so neither the name nor a count is confirmed today.

claims.claim: Terminal 3 due to open in 2026
claims.note: Hunan Daily (28 January 2026, from the Changsha government portal): T3 is 533,600 square metres, more than twice T1 and T2 together, due in 2026, linked to maglev, high-speed rail and metro, for 40 million passengers a year. Wikipedia (19 September 2026) has only the east terminal area 'in which both Terminals 3 and 4 lie'; People's Daily (2019) has the 2019 master plan for four terminals. Nothing saved says it has opened.

quote: the T3 terminal is scheduled for operation in 2026
designed to handle an annual passenger throughput of 40 million

claims.why: Held back: a new terminal that replaces nothing in the old text while it is still being built, so the sweep's rule keeps it out. Andy may want it in, as it will change which terminal clients use: 'A third terminal, more than twice the size of the other two together, is due to open in 2026, so check which terminal a client will use.' Only one source dates the opening (Hunan Daily).
